programTitle: Kalshi MLB market-structure, relative-value, information and execution inefficiency research

evidenceTiers.TIER_A_CONFIRMATORY: Rows drawn only from snapshots the repository classifies research-qualified COMPLETE (lib.edgelab.capture_completeness). At registry freeze: 2 snapshots, both 2026-09-22 morning, zero settled rows.
evidenceTiers.TIER_B_EXPLORATORY: PARTIAL / UNKNOWN_LEGACY observation rows, the recovered exchange record (1-minute candles + trade tape, ticker universe conditioned on the observation archive), the multi-book slate captures, and the research-branch prospective corpus captured under the ALPHA-0002 collector whose delivered cadence (3-8 runs/day) never met its own health gate. Missing markets are never treated as absent markets.
evidenceTiers.TIER_C_PROSPECTIVE: COMPLETE captures taken after a spec in this registry is frozen with a hash.

globalRules.interval: game-clustered bootstrap CI90 (2000 resamples, seed 20260922); null-centred cluster-bootstrap p-value where a p-value is reported
globalRules.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.10 applied WITHIN each multiplicityFamily over every test registered in that family (including tests that end up DATA_BLOCKED, which count toward the search space but contribute no p)
globalRules.executionModel: BUY YES at yesAsk, BUY NO at noAsk when archived else 100 - yesBid; taker fee lib.edgelab.kalshi_fees.taker_fee (0.07*C*P*(1-P), rounded up to the cent); maker leg reported at 0.0175 (conservative) and 0.0 (optimistic), never pooled; USD 10 whole-contract order; midpoint is never a fill; top-of-book only unless a depth ladder is archived (prospective books)
globalRules.candidateBar: a test becomes CANDIDATE only if (a) BH survivor in its family, (b) post-fee executable effect with CI90 excluding 0 AND point estimate >= +1.0% of cash risked (or >= +1.0 cent for price-move targets), (c) sample floor met, (d) stable sign across the first and second half of dates, (e) plausible mechanism recorded, (f) no reliance on a midpoint fill or an unarchived quote
globalRules.productionAuthority: NONE. Nothing in this registry changes production eligibility, thresholds, staking, bankroll, recommendations or execution.
globalRules.rawEvidence: Raw archives are read-only. All outputs are derived artifacts under data/edgelab/research_artifacts/market_structure/.

hypotheses.title: Total-ladder monotonicity at 1-minute resolution
hypotheses.statement: Within one KXMLBTOTAL or KXMLBF5TOTAL ladder, P(total >= N) must be non-increasing in N. An executable violation is bid(N+1) > ask(N) (buy YES N, buy NO N+1) after taker fees on both legs.
hypotheses.data: recovered 1-minute candles 2026-08-02..08-31 (TIER_B); minute closes of yes_bid/yes_ask; pregame minutes only
hypotheses.primaryMetric: count and share of ladder-minutes with a post-fee executable violation; total locked profit in cents per pair
hypotheses.method: exhaustive constraint check; no inference needed for existence; RV follow-up in MRV-COH-006
hypotheses.failureCriterion: zero post-fee executable violations, or violations that never persist for >= 2 consecutive minutes
hypotheses.priorWork: MLB-ALPHA-0001 Family B found 0 executable inversions in 103,409 pairs on the coarse archive (hours cadence). This test asks whether the coarse cadence hid transient inversions.

results.summary: 0 pre-fee and 0 post-fee inversions in 1348014 game-total + 248534 F5-total ladder pairs at 1-minute resolution; adjacent rungs sit 6-14c apart
results.execution: same-minute candle closes, YES at ask, NO at 100-bid

hypotheses.title: Three-way winner sum bounds (F3/F5/F7) at 1-minute resolution
hypotheses.statement: For an inning-segment winner market with AWAY, HOME and TIE contracts, sum of asks < 100 (buy all three YES) or sum of bids > 100 (buy all three NO) is an arbitrage after fees.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: count of post-fee executable sum violations
hypotheses.priorWork: Family B: 0 violations in 719 batches on coarse archive

results.summary: pre-fee sum violations exist (F5 668/16031, F3 2644/10039, F7 938/8032 event-minutes; asks summing 98-99 or bids 101-102) but 0 survive taker fees on three legs
results.execution: same-minute candle closes, YES at ask, NO at 100-bid

hypotheses.title: Cross-horizon dominance: F5 total >= N implies full-game total >= N
hypotheses.statement: P(F5 total >= N) <= P(game total >= N) for every N. Executable violation: bid(KXMLBF5TOTAL-N) > ask(KXMLBTOTAL-N) after fees (buy YES game-total N, buy NO F5-total N).
hypotheses.data: recovered candles 2026-08-02..08-31 (TIER_B), matched on physical game and rung
hypotheses.primaryMetric: count of post-fee executable violations; distribution of the pre-fee slack ask(TOTAL-N) - bid(F5TOTAL-N)
hypotheses.priorWork: not tested by Family B (it compared only within-series ladders, spread-vs-ML, TT-vs-GT, hits-vs-HRR)

results.summary: 0 pre-fee and 0 post-fee violations in 182721 F5-total vs game-total rung pairs (first test of this constraint)
results.execution: same-minute candle closes, YES at ask, NO at 100-bid

hypotheses.title: YES/NO book parity
hypotheses.statement: On Kalshi a NO order at price q is a YES order at 100-q on the same book, so noAsk + yesBid = 100 and noBid + yesAsk = 100 must hold exactly. Any deviation in the archive is a capture artifact, not an opportunity.
hypotheses.data: registry snapshots Era B (2026-09-10..09-22) carrying no_bid/no_ask (TIER_B)
hypotheses.primaryMetric: share of rows violating parity
hypotheses.failureCriterion: any violation is classified as data defect; hypothesis is REJECTED as a source of edge if parity holds

results.summary: by exchange construction a NO order at q is a YES order at 100-q on the same book; the prospective order books carry only YES/NO resting bids and the runners derive the NO ask as 100-yesBid, so parity cannot fail except as a capture artifact; no edge

hypotheses.title: Team-total vs game-total and run-line vs moneyline dominance on September captures
hypotheses.statement: P(team runs >= N) <= P(game total >= N); P(team wins by > k) <= P(team wins). Executable violations after fees. Out-of-sample replication of Family B on 2026-09-01..09-22 captures.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: count of post-fee executable violations

results.summary: 0 violations in 102092 team-total vs game-total and 72205 spread vs moneyline pairs (exchange record 08-02..08-07 for those families); September registry replication not run because the collector captured <=30 game-total books
results.execution: same-minute candle closes, YES at ask, NO at 100-bid

hypotheses.title: Near-arbitrage relative value: pre-fee ladder inversions close, and the corrective pair pays
hypotheses.statement: When a within-ladder pre-fee inversion bid(N+1) >= ask(N) appears at minute t, (a) the inversion closes within 30 minutes more often than a matched non-inverted control, and (b) buying the corrective pair at executable prices earns post-fee settlement P/L > 0.
hypotheses.unit: episode (first minute of inversion per ladder pair); game cluster
hypotheses.primaryMetric: post-fee settlement P/L per USD risked on corrective pair, CI90 clustered; secondary: closure rate at +30 min
hypotheses.method: episode study, game-clustered bootstrap, BH within MF-COH
hypotheses.failureCriterion: P/L CI includes 0 or point estimate < +1%
hypotheses.priorWork: Family B: corrective RV trades lost -38.7% (p=0.0005) on coarse archive

results.summary: no pre-fee within-ladder inversion episode occurred in 94,231 pregame game-minutes, so there is nothing to trade or to measure convergence on
results.execution: same-minute candle closes, YES at ask, NO at 100-bid

hypotheses.title: Full-game moneyline leads F5 moneyline (same team) at 5/15/30-minute horizons
hypotheses.statement: Lagged change in KXMLBGAME fair-mid predicts the next-horizon change in the same team's KXMLBF5 fair-mid after controlling for F5's own lagged change (partial correlation). Three horizons predeclared: 5, 15, 30 minutes.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: partial regression coefficient of dB(t,t+h) on dA(t-h,t) controlling dB(t-h,t); clustered CI90; null-centred p
hypotheses.method: pooled OLS with game-clustered bootstrap; 3 tests (one per horizon) registered
hypotheses.failureCriterion: coefficient CI includes 0 at every horizon, or the implied move is below spread+fee
hypotheses.priorWork: ALPHA-0002 Family C tested within-contract features only; cross-family lead/lag untested

results.execution: partial slope on fair mids; a positive slope below spread+fee is price discovery, not a trade

hypotheses.title: Kalshi moneyline converges toward Pinnacle no-vig probability
hypotheses.statement: Signed disagreement d = p_pinnacle_novig - kalshi_fair_mid at capture t predicts the change in Kalshi fair-mid to the next capture and to the last pregame capture (slope > 0).
hypotheses.data: research-branch prospective corpus 2026-09-02..09-22: odds (Pinnacle h2h decimal, book last_update) + quotes (yesBid/yesAsk) captured in the same run (TIER_B); as-of = capturedAt; pregame only
hypotheses.primaryMetric: OLS slope of dMid on d, clustered CI90
hypotheses.method: pooled regression; 2 horizons registered (next capture, last pregame)
hypotheses.priorWork: ALPHA-0002 D2: slope 0.12-0.28, CIs include 0 at 20 games (INSUFFICIENT); this is the first run at >= 200 games

results.summary: Pinnacle-vs-Kalshi ML: mean |d| 0.42pp, never >=2pp; slope of Kalshi move to next capture 0.21 CI[-0.05,0.44], to last pregame 0.47 CI[-0.02,0.90] (133 games, 20 dates, median 275 min to next capture); price discovery only
results.timingCaveat: capturedAt is the run start; the Odds API leg is fetched later in the same run (book last_update can be a few minutes NEWER than the Kalshi book), so a small part of any same-run disagreement may already be stale on the Kalshi side; horizons are hours, which bounds the contamination

hypotheses.title: Taking Pinnacle's side on Kalshi at |disagreement| >= 3pp is profitable after fees
hypotheses.statement: When |d| >= 3 percentage points (threshold preregistered by ALPHA-0002 D3, not tuned here), a USD 10 taker order on Pinnacle's side at the executable Kalshi price earns post-fee settlement P/L > 0 and positive executable CLV to the last pregame quote.
hypotheses.data: same corpus as MRV-XV-001 joined to settlements (TIER_B)
hypotheses.unit: game-capture episode (first qualifying capture per game-side); game cluster
hypotheses.primaryMetric: post-fee settlement ROI on cash risked, CI90; secondary executable CLV cents
hypotheses.method: episode study, clustered bootstrap, BH within MF-XV

results.summary: 0 episodes: |Pinnacle - Kalshi| never reached the preregistered 3pp (max <2pp; break-even |d| for a hold-to-settlement taker is ~5.9pp given the fitted convergence slope)

hypotheses.title: Settlement calibration of the last pregame executable price by spread and volume bucket
hypotheses.statement: Buying YES at the last pregame ask has different post-fee ROI in wide-spread (>= 4c) vs tight (<= 2c) books and in low-volume (bottom tercile) vs high-volume books, within family.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: post-fee ROI difference wide-tight and low-high, clustered CI90; 2 tests registered

results.summary: BUY-YES post-fee ROI wide(>=4c) minus tight(<=2c) spread -0.180 CI[-0.263,-0.088]; low minus high volume tercile -0.029 CI[-0.098,0.034] (274 games, 21 dates); wide books lose MORE, i.e. no inefficiency to harvest, just higher cost

hypotheses.title: MLB-RSCH-0026 preregistered forward score and rerun
hypotheses.statement: Score settle-date > 2026-08-28 rows with the frozen beta=0.9833 shrink (never refit) vs raw fair mid on Brier/log loss with game-clustered CI; and, since the archive now exceeds the preregistered 1,000 rows / 60 games rerun threshold, refit beta on a September TRAIN window and validate on the later September window under the original gates.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: paired Brier delta shrunk - market, CI90; beta CI excludes 1
hypotheses.method: as frozen in data/edgelab/analytics/frozen_mlb_rsch_0026_forward_model.json; 1 forward test + 1 rerun registered
hypotheses.failureCriterion: beta CI includes 1 or Brier delta CI includes 0

results.summary: frozen beta=0.9833 forward (settle > 08-28, 17540 rows / 274 games): shrunk minus market Brier +0.000053 CI[+0.000009,+0.000097] (shrink hurts or is null); preregistered rerun: beta_train=0.974 CI[0.912,1.045], VAL Brier delta +0.000138 CI[+0.000052,+0.000219], gates beta-CI-excludes-1=False VAL-delta-negative=False -> not both

forward.note: both forecasts clamped to [0.01,0.99] symmetrically; population = all settled non-prop rows with a two-sided last pregame quote (broader than RSCH-0026's production-evaluated corpus)

hypotheses.title: Price-band post-fee ROI of BUY YES and BUY NO at the last pregame quote, September, by family
hypotheses.statement: Out-of-sample replication of ALPHA-0001 Family A on 2026-09-01..09-21: five fixed price bands (0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80, 80-100 cents of the executable price) x two sides x nine non-prop families. Reported in full; BH within MF-PB.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: post-fee ROI per band, clustered CI90
hypotheses.method: clustered bootstrap, BH q=0.10 over all cells in MF-PB
hypotheses.failureCriterion: no cell survives BH with ROI >= +1%

results.summary: 73 family x side x band cells on 274 games / 21 dates (median last quote 96 min before start); BH survivors 16, of which 0 positive-ROI cells meet the candidate bar: none

hypotheses.title: Executable depth and slippage at size
hypotheses.statement: Descriptive: from archived order books, the fill price and slippage for USD 10 / 50 / 100 / 250 taker orders by family and side, and the share of books where a USD 100 order cannot fill within 2 cents of the top.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: slippage cents per order size

results.summary: 34819 pregame books / 289 games: median top-of-book depth 750 contracts at the ask, USD 100 YES order fills within 2c of top in 82% of books, USD 250 unfilled in 3.7%; depth is not the binding constraint for USD 10-100 orders, spread+fee are
results.caveat: collector capped at 400 books per run, so KXMLBTOTAL/SPREAD/TEAMTOTAL books are nearly absent; cells reflect the captured families only; sizes are Kalshi fp contracts; slippage excludes fees

hypotheses.title: Where the money leaks: taker mark-to-mid decomposition from the trade tape
hypotheses.statement: For every pregame taker print, decompose the taker's expected loss into (i) half-spread at execution, (ii) taker fee, (iii) subsequent fair-mid drift at +5, +30 minutes and last pregame minute (adverse or favourable). Aggregated by family, price band and lead-time bucket. Positive drift toward the taker means informed flow; negative means makers earn beyond the spread.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: cents per contract of each component; clustered CI90 on drift by family (6 families registered)
hypotheses.method: descriptive accounting + clustered CI, BH within MF-EXEC on the drift-to-close test
hypotheses.failureCriterion: drift CI includes 0 (then the leak is purely spread + fee)

results.summary: 1985438 pregame prints / 391 games: taker pays half-spread 0.58c + fee 1.68c per contract; fair mid then drifts 0.33c TOWARD the taker by last pregame minute (volume-weighted); net taker edge at last pregame -1.93c; drift BH survivors: ['game_result', 'game_total', 'inning_result', 'inning_total', 'team_total', 'winning_margin']
results.conventions: cents per contract, volume-weighted by count_fp; pregame prints only; pre-trade mid = candle close one minute before the print; drift signed toward the taker; taker fee 0.07*P*(1-P) unrounded; maker fee at 0.0175 (conservative)

hypotheses.title: Maker realized spread by family
hypotheses.statement: Mirror of MRV-EXEC-002 from the maker's side: half-spread earned minus adverse drift to +30 minutes minus maker fee (0.0175 and 0.0 reported). Identifies families where passive liquidity provision is compensated.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: maker realized spread cents, clustered CI90 (6 families)

results.summary: maker realized spread at +30 min (half-spread earned minus adverse drift minus 0.0175 maker fee), volume-weighted: all -0.04c; BH survivors by family: []

hypotheses.title: Within-game outcome correlation structure
hypotheses.statement: Descriptive: pairwise phi correlation of settlement outcomes between families of the same game (ML, F5 ML, RL, totals, F5 totals, team totals) and the effective number of independent bets for a uniform one-contract-per-family position. No inference.
hypotheses.primaryMetric: phi matrix; effective N

results.summary: 662 games with all six canonical contracts: phi ML~F5ML 0.58, ML~RL2 0.71, TOTAL8~F5TOTAL5 0.53, TOTAL8~TT4 0.46; six one-contract positions behave like ~2.3 independent bets
